title: Which statements are true?
source: School paper, Q21 (statements B and D are not in the syllabus LO list)
stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true about magnets?

  • A Unlike poles of two magnets will attract each other.
  • B The strength of a magnet does not depend on its size.
  • C All metals can be made into magnets using the electrical method.
  • D Dropping a magnet from a height many times can cause a magnet to lose its magnetism.

options.pick: A is a rule everyone remembers. C sounds true because the electrical method makes a magnet from a nail, and a nail is a metal.
options.why: C is false: only iron and steel can be made into magnets. Aluminium and copper are metals, but they cannot be made into magnets. B and D are also true, so “A and C only” is wrong twice.

options.pick: A is true and B is a believable-sounding fact about strength. Many students stop here because D seems unlikely.
options.why: A and B are true, but D is true as well. Dropping a magnet many times can weaken it, so “A and B only” leaves one out.

options.pick: Check each statement. A is true (unlike poles attract). B is true (size alone does not decide how strong a magnet is). C is false (only iron and steel). D is true (dropping can weaken a magnet).
options.why: Correct: A, B and D are true. C is false because only iron or steel can be made into magnets.

options.pick: B and D are true. C is believed because the electrical method is described as working on metals.
options.why: This choice leaves out A. Unlike poles (N and S) attract, so A is true. C is false because only iron and steel can be made into magnets.

title: Which can be made into a magnet?
stem:
Four objects are made of different metals.

  • P a steel screw
  • Q a strip of aluminium foil
  • R a copper wire
  • S an iron nail

Which objects can be made into magnets using the electrical method?

options.pick: Only iron or steel can be made into a magnet. P is steel and S is iron.
options.why: Correct: steel and iron can be made into magnets. Aluminium and copper cannot.

options.pick: They are shiny metals, and metals are the things that magnets work on.
options.why: A magnet does not act on aluminium or copper, and they cannot be made into magnets.

options.pick: Three of the objects are metals that look similar to iron and steel.
options.why: Aluminium (Q) is a metal, but it cannot be made into a magnet. Only iron and steel can.

options.pick: All four are metals, and the electrical method is for metals.
options.why: Only iron or steel can be made into magnets, not every metal.

title: Poles that attract and repel
stem:
Four statements are made about two bar magnets.

  • A Two N poles attract each other.
  • B An N pole and an S pole attract each other.
  • C Two S poles repel each other.
  • D An N pole and an S pole repel each other.

Which statements are true?

options.pick: Two of the same pole are alike, so they seem to attract. C then sounds right too.
options.why: Like poles repel. Two N poles repel, so A is false. B is true as well.

options.pick: Unlike poles attract (N and S), and like poles repel (two S poles).
options.why: Correct: B and C are true. Unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

options.pick: The words “attract” and “repel” are swapped around.
options.why: This swaps the two rules. Unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

options.pick: B is true. D is picked because a push can be between any two poles.
options.why: An N pole and an S pole are unlike poles, so they attract, and D is false. C is true.

title: A magnet that was dropped
source: Not in the syllabus LO list (losing magnetism); tested in the school paper
stem:
A bar magnet picked up 8 paper clips. It was dropped on the floor many times. It then picked up only 3 paper clips.

What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Dropping it changed it into a magnetic material.
options.pick: A magnetic material is attracted to a magnet but is weaker, so it seems to fit.
options.why: A magnet that is dropped is still a magnet. It has become weaker. It still has two poles and can still attract and repel.

options.pick: A magnet does not change, so something else must have changed.
options.why: The paper clips did not change. Their mass is the same. The magnet is the part that changed.

options.text: Its poles moved to the middle of the magnet.
options.pick: The magnet looks the same, so maybe its poles shifted.
options.why: The poles of a bar magnet stay at its ends. Dropping the magnet did not move them.

options.text: Dropping it many times weakened its magnetism.
options.pick: A magnet can lose some of its magnetism if it is dropped, hit or heated.
options.why: Correct: dropping a magnet many times can cause it to lose its magnetism, so it picks up fewer paper clips.

title: Hammered magnet
source: Not in the syllabus LO list (losing magnetism); tested in the school paper
stem:
Kai's magnet used to pick up 12 steel nails. He hit it hard with a hammer many times. It now picks up only 4 nails.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The magnet has lost some of its magnetism.
options.pick: Hitting a magnet many times can weaken it.
options.why: Correct: hitting a magnet hard many times can weaken it, so it picks up fewer nails.

options.text: The magnet has turned into a magnetic material.
options.pick: It still picks up some nails, but fewer, so it seems to have changed into a weaker kind of object.
options.why: It is still a magnet with two poles, but a weaker one. Hitting it did not change what kind of object it is.

options.text: The magnet cannot change, so Kai must have used the wrong nails.
options.pick: Magnets always keep their strength.
options.why: A magnet can lose some magnetism. It was the same nails as before.

options.pick: Lighter nails would be easier to lift.
options.why: The nails did not change. The magnet did.

title: Weakening a magnet
source: Not in the syllabus LO list (losing magnetism); tested in the school paper
stem: Which of these could cause a magnet to lose some of its magnetism?

options.pick: A compass is a small magnet, so it seems to act on the magnet.
options.why: A compass does not weaken a magnet.

options.text: Using it to pick up steel paper clips.
options.pick: Using a magnet a lot seems to use it up.
options.why: Picking up paper clips does not weaken a magnet.

options.pick: Rough treatment can disturb a magnet.
options.why: Correct: dropping a magnet many times can cause it to lose some of its magnetism.

options.text: Putting it next to a plastic ruler.
options.pick: A plastic ruler is a different material, so it may have an effect.
options.why: Plastic does not have any effect on a magnet.
